facts.statement: The key-findings publication was updated 22 July 2026.
The publication applies to England.
Connectivity findings are stated as of July 2026.
Most-rural areas trail the rest of England for decent broadband.
Most-rural areas trail the rest of England for superfast broadband.
Most-rural areas trail the rest of England for gigabit-capable broadband.
Majority-rural constituencies have proportionally more voice/text not-spots.
Majority-rural constituencies have proportionally more 4G not-spots.
Majority-rural constituencies have proportionally more 5G not-spots.
The more rural the area, the greater reliance on car or van travel.
More-rural populations tend to travel farther.
Majority-rural authorities are less likely to have plug-in vehicles.
Public charging provision is proportionally higher per vehicle in rural authorities.
Rural areas have poorer connectivity to services than urban areas.
Non-driving access is particularly disadvantaged in rural areas.
Rural working-from-home share is 35%.
Urban working-from-home share is 30%.
Rural working-from-home share exceeds urban by 5 percentage points.
Rural connectivity context supports prioritisation, not exact parcel truth.
Exact parcel availability still requires source-level UPRN evidence.
